sources.entry: AI Research Skills by Wenyu Chiou - A catalog of 15 Claude Code skills mapped to 8 research-workflow stages (literature → gap analysis → design → drafting → reviewer response), where each stage emits an explicit YAML/Markdown deliverable the next stage consumes. Thoughtfully designed around anti-hallucination — schemas force "gap" status on unsupported claims, and downstream skills refuse malforme

summary.one_liner: A catalog and installer for 17 portable Claude Code (and other agent host) skills that walk research work through an eight-stage lifecycle, with YAML/Markdown handoffs between stages and human gates before consequential steps.
summary.what_it_does: Provides 17 SKILL.md contracts, grouped into 12 skills in the research-workspace plugin and others in four standalone plugins (academic-writing, paper-review, zotero-skills, codex-delegate, antigravity-delegate). Skills cover literature discovery and triage, a three-gate go/no-go check on candidate gaps, research design dialog, project manifests in .research/ so new AI sessions can re-orient, and manuscript claim tracking in .paper/claims.yml. The README states that claims with no evidence artifacts must be marked status: gap with a gap_reason, and that downstream skills can reject malformed handoffs. It also describes an optional research-hub Python CLI (pip install research-hub-pipeline) for resumable literature runs that can use Zotero, Obsidian and NotebookLM when available. Routing across Claude, Codex and Antigravity is handled by a separate multi-AI skill. The repo is also a registry: its docs describe how to install the skills into non-Claude hosts such as Hermes, Codex CLI and Cursor.
use_cases: compare several papers by method, data and limitations
decide whether a research gap is worth a thesis or proposal
maintain persistent research context across AI sessions
track manuscript claims and their evidence
prepare reviewer responses and audit manuscript prose
automate a live literature search and ingest into Zotero or Obsidian
stack: arXiv and Semantic Scholar search (via research-hub)
notable: Eight-stage research lifecycle where each stage's output file is the next stage's input
Schema rule that forces status: gap on claims without evidence, so unsupported claims are not marked supported
Explicit human gates for semantic acceptance, external writes and release authorization
Portable SKILL.md contracts usable outside Claude Code, with a documented Hermes skill-load check for one skill
Character-based routing that sends bounded mechanical coding work to Codex or Antigravity and keeps judgment with the primary model
caveats: Written and tested by one graduate-student researcher; not validated at corpus scale
Domain bias toward water resources and agent-based modeling; not validated for social sciences, ML or clinical writing
Behavior on real inputs depends on the source repos of each plugin; no claude plugin install round-trip is asserted by CI
Live research-hub runs make network calls, model calls and writes, and the README requires authorization before running them
Only some non-Claude hosts are verified (Hermes for one skill); OpenClaw and others are not release-verified
